Helios Cloud · fictional operator · dcforecast 0.1.0

Data-center power forecasting and carbon-aware scheduling

Probabilistic 24-hour-ahead forecasts (P10 / P50 / P90) of facility power for 6 sites, trained on a laptop GPU and turned into energy, cost and carbon decisions. All data is synthetic and generated by a documented, physically-motivated model; every number below comes from a real pipeline run.

1. Telemetry and data quality

Hourly facility power = IT load x PUE, where PUE rises with outside temperature once a site leaves its free-cooling regime. Sensor faults (gaps, spikes, stuck values) are injected and then detected and imputed by the cleaning step.

2. Forecast vs actual

Production model LSTM enc-dec (best backtest mase = 0.4043) on the last backtest fold: daily 24-hour-ahead forecasts issued at 00:00 UTC with a P10-P90 band.

3. Rolling-origin backtest

4 folds; each model is refit on all data before the fold and forecasts every day of the test window. MASE is scaled by the in-sample seasonal-naive (24 h) error; coverage is the share of actuals inside the P10-P90 band (target 80%).

5. From forecast to decisions

Next 72 hours from 2025-12-31T23:00 UTC. The P50 forecast is converted into energy, cost and carbon per site; then 120 MWh of deferrable batch compute is placed by a linear program under per-site power caps.

6. Method notes

  • Features are leakage-safe: every lag is at least 24 h old at forecast time and rolling statistics use only the past. Weather covariates assume a day-ahead weather forecast is available when the forecast is issued (the generator stores a noisy forecast next to the truth).
  • Deep models are global (one network for all sites, with a site embedding) and forecast all 24 horizons at once with a pinball loss on P10 / P50 / P90.
  • Training uses AMP on CUDA, pinned memory, gradient clipping, OneCycle LR, early stopping with checkpointing and a VRAM-aware batch-size finder that keeps well inside a shared 4 GB GPU.
  • The scheduler is an LP (scipy HiGHS): move deferrable energy into low-carbon (or low-cost) hours and, for a portable share, to other sites, without exceeding facility power caps.
